exposure: Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal birth, induced vaginal birth, elective caesarean section)
cohort: Pregnant women at gestational week 16-18 recruited to the BASIC study at Uppsala University Hospital, Sweden, divided into three groups: spontaneous vaginal birth (n=45), induced vaginal birth (n=45), and elective caesarean section (n=45).
finding: Women experiencing term vaginal births, both spontaneous and induced, exhibited elevated levels of dimethylarginines (ADMA and SDMA) and lower levels of L-arginine compared to those undergoing elective caesarean sections.
mod_finding: Women with induced vaginal birth had higher ADMA and lower L-arginine, L-arginine/ADMA, and L-arginine/SDMA compared to women with spontaneous vaginal birth.
gest_age: Term (gestational week 16-18 at recruitment, samples taken at start of labor)
